quoted: If the storage medium for the file permits rewinding, the following rules apply [GR9, cite.py OK]; When the NO REWIND phrase is specified, execution of the OPEN statement does not cause the file to be repositioned [GR9, cite.py OK]; Treatment of sequential mass storage files is logically equivalent to the treatment of a file on tape or analogous sequential media [XIII.4.2.4 preamble, cite.py OK; the same sentence is VII.4.2.4, cite.py OK]; A file whose output medium is such that the concepts of rewind and reels/units have no meaning [XIII.4.2.4 GR2a, cite.py OK]; for an OPEN statement with the NO REWIND phrase, the referenced file is on a non-reel/unit medium [VII.1.3.5, cite.py OK]; When files are opened with the INPUT or I-O phrase, the file position indicator is set to 1 [VII.4.3.4 GR14, cite.py OK]
reason: The closed set ('no medium WiseOwl supports at 85 permits rewinding') is opened by the 1985 text itself. The Report Writer CLOSE general rules (and the Sequential I-O ones, word for word) say that 'Treatment of sequential mass storage files is logically equivalent to the treatment of a file on tape or analogous sequential media', and define the non-reel/unit category as a medium on which 'the concepts of rewind and reels/units have no meaning'. A report file is a sequential mass storage file (one host path, SequentialConnector), so the 1985 text treats it as a tape file: a sequential single-reel/unit file, on which rewind has meaning, i.e. a medium that permits rewinding. GR9 then applies, and GR9b (OPEN WITH NO REWIND does not reposition) is a successful OPEN on a reel/unit medium, status 00; status 07 is reserved by VII.1.3.5 for a non-reel/unit medium. The compiler classes every sequential connector NonUnit (SequentialConnector.cs:1125, whose 'FORCED, not chosen' remark argues from the 2023 status 07 and Table 14, i.e. from the classification it is meant to justify) and prints 07 (probe r9rewind: RPT-OPEN-NO-REWIND 07, RPT-CLOSE-NO-REWIND 07; the sequential file likewise gives 07 for CLOSE NO REWIND and CLOSE REEL, and reads BBBB after CLOSE REEL where a single-reel tape would give at end). So the witness is r9rewind's report-file OPEN OUTPUT WITH NO REWIND: derived 00, observed 07. The drafted 1985 register entry ('Every physical file ... is on a non-reel/unit medium ... No such medium permits rewinding') contradicts VII.4.2.4 and XIII.4.2.4 and must not be filed as drafted. On GR9a: its plain effect is not witnessable on its own: for a report file (OUTPUT or EXTEND only) a non-EXTEND OPEN is OUTPUT, whose created file is empty, so 'positioned at its beginning' is the creation rule's consequent; for the Sequential I-O twin (VII.4.3.4 GR11a) the first READ after OPEN INPUT returning the first record is GR14's consequent (position indicator set to 1). So GR9a alone does not overturn; GR9b with the tape-equivalence sentence does.

The only clock sources are DateTimeOffset.Now and the WISEOWL_COBOL_CLOCK pin (Clock.cs:38-42), both full DateTimeOffsets. Tried: unpinned (FRAC 71), pinned to a whole second (FRAC 00, the fraction IS zero, which RV1 and RV2 both give), and an unparseable pin (silently falls back to the system clock, FRAC 61; a separate fail-loudly concern, not this rule). No state yields a system without the facility, so no program's output depends on RV2.

quoted: If vertical positioning is not applicable on the hardware device [GR10, cite.py OK]
reason: The antecedent is a DISPLAY device without vertical positioning. The device-name table (ImplementorNames.Build, no edition argument) has four devices: CONSOLE (in/out), SYSIN (in), SYSOUT (out), SYSERR (out, standard error), plus features C01/CSP and switches. Tried at --std 85: DISPLAY UPON a C01 mnemonic is refused (COBOL0817, r610disp); DISPLAY with no UPON, UPON CONSOLE and UPON SYSERR all go to line streams and position to the next line (r610disp2: 'LINE1LINE2' then 'LINE3' on stdout, 'ERR1' on stderr; NO ADVANCING suppresses it as specified). No reachable device lacks vertical positioning. Arm fits (subject is the operating system, so definitional is not open).

reason: The closed set ('no read of a report group's storage not preceded by its own formatting') has a member: the sum counter. SR10d lets a program reference an entry's data-name exactly when the entry defines a sum counter, GR6 lets Procedure Division statements use it, and the counter persists across the formatting of OTHER groups (it accumulates over every GENERATE). The draft excludes it by saying the counter is 'a separate compiler-generated item ... outside the group's area', but no 1985 sentence puts the counter outside the area of the 01 entry that describes it: XIII.3.19.4 GR1 says only that it is compiler-generated, and GR5 makes the entry's data-name the counter's name, i.e. the counter is the item that entry, subordinate to its 01, defines. If the 01 entries of an RD were implicit redefinitions of one area (the FD rule), formatting a DETAIL group would overwrite the CONTROL FOOTING group's counter. Witness r314rd at --std 85: DETAIL DL (SOURCE X(10), SOURCE 9(4) at column 12) and CONTROL FOOTING FINAL with TOT PIC 9(6) SUM WS-AMT at column 12; three GENERATE DL with 1111, 2222, 3333, DISPLAY TOT after each.
